messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Elevated 5xx / gateway timeouts observed for private-vpc egress (us-west-2). 5m error rate increased from ~3% to ~22%. Affected: several private deployments behind shared NAT pools. Paging oncall: @alice (oncall)

alice (oncall): taking this. opening thread. anyone see correlation with deploys?

ben: I see repeated 504/502s from the inference-gateway. Traces show TCP resets to upstream egress (10.48.2.0/24 -> provider-nat). Sample log: ```2026-03-15T01:23:15Z gateway service_id=gw-34 req_id=abc123 upstream=10.48.2.17 status=504 message="upstream reset"```

carla: checking VPC NAT metrics now. Cloud console shows SNAT port allocation at 87% for nat-pool-west-1, conntrack count trending up. No recent infra PRs for SGs in last 6h.

dmitri: any peering route flaps in control plane? I saw a warning earlier but didn't connect it.

eve: I pulled peering logs, there are intermittent BGP withdraws flagged in provider's status around 01:18-01:25. marking that suspicious. No security group edits in our audit.

ben: attaching a short tcpdump from a bastion for context: ```18:24:12.345 IP gw-ephemeral.34567 > 3.120.45.200.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0``` lots of SYN but fewer ACKs back.

carla: here's conntrack snapshot (truncated): ```tcp      6 431999 ESTABLISHED src=10.48.2.17 dst=3.120.45.200 sport=54321 dport=443 ...``` we have many half-open-ish states. ephemeral port exhaustion is likely.

alice (oncall): ok immediate mitigation plan: 1) move critical customer routes to fallback-egress route table (force different NAT target) 2) spin up a dedicated NAT gateway in same AZ and add to route table 3) limit connection reuse timeouts for gateway service as quick patch. Who can do 1 & 2?

infra-bot: NAT autoscale check: current nat-gw count=2, target_min=2, scaling_disabled=false. No autoscale events in last 12h.

dmitri: I'll create a temporary dedicated NAT and add to private route table for the hot subnets. ETA 6-8m.

deploy-bot: route-table update job queued: rt-0a1b2 -> add target nat-alloc-2135 (manual fallback).

ben: I'm going to flip gateway service keepalive to 30s to reduce half-open linger, will revert after stability. Patch: ```sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30``` applying to gateway pods now.

carla: also adding a short conntrack purge script to reclaim stuck entries for the worst-hit hosts. running on pool nodes.```for ip in $(cat hosts); do conntrack -D -s $ip; done```

alice (oncall): route change applied by deploy-bot, new nat allocated by dmitri is attached. rolling healthchecks now.

ben: after keepalive tweak + new nat, 5xx trending down: 22% -> 7% in last 3m. latency for affected routes also improving.

eve: provider reports their peering instability cleared at 01:29. might be two contributing factors (peering flap + NAT port pressure).

carla: customer impact note: inner-tenant inference requests for 4 customers experienced degraded throughput and ~20% error increase for ~25 minutes (01:15-01:40). I've started an incident ticket with customer IDs and timelines.

alice (oncall): good work. current status: degraded -> degraded(stabilizing). Action items: - carla to file incident ticket + customer notifications - dmitri to keep dedicated NAT for 24h and monitor port usage - infra to enable NAT autoscale policy tweak for ephemeral port limits - ben to revert tcp_fin_timeout after 1h if stable - postmortem assigned to alice + carla + dmitri.

dmitri: NAT left in place and monitoring. adding alert if ephemeral usage >80% for 15m.

infra-bot: alert rule created: nat-ephemeral-usage > 80% for 15m -> page infra oncall.

ben: reverting keepalive soon, but leaving conntrack purge cron for 2h.

alice (oncall): error rate at ~4% now, windows showing normalizing. closing active paging at ~01:51 but keeping thread live for follow-ups and PM. :white_check_mark:

carla: saving logs and putting links into incident ticket. will draft customer-facing blurb and escalate to SRE lead.

incident-bot: Incident recorded: INC-2026-0315-03. Severity: Sev2. Assigned: alice, carla, dmitri. Timeline note added.

alice (oncall): thanks all. postmortem to include: root cause analysis of provider peering events + our NAT capacity plan and better failover routing. I'll schedule a 1hr review tomorrow.
